name: The LISABO turned across the room, parallel to the living room: 32in on the living-room side, 26in under the buffet
notes:
Alternative, 2026-10-26, for Andrew's question ("why can't we flip the orientation of the table? can we?"): a's LISABO 78 3/4" ash turned across the room, parallel to the living room, x 30-108.75, y 62.25-93: its kitchen end on that walkway's edge (F-42), 19 1/4" of dead floor at the right wall (no seat fits there), 32.25" from its living-room side to that walkway's edge (the chairs there sit with their backs to the living room, 11" inside the clearance, and push back into the walkway by about 9" when someone stands up) and 26" from its other side to the bottom wall (tight:26, F-36; those chairs push back under the floating buffet, 33" up, and nobody passes behind them). Four chairs two a side; Maddie's URBAN between the living-room pair, where a parent on the walkway reaches her; six seats fit along the sides later.
Against a (the table along the room's depth): 32 and 26" on the chair sides instead of 33.6" on both; the long side toward the living room, so the table reads wide from the sofa, instead of toward the kitchen; the cook steps from the kitchen to the table's end instead of its side; and the table runs across the oak floor's grain toward the kitchen's tile line instead of parallel to it. Both work; a keeps both walkways cleaner.
Everything else as in a: the pendant over the table's center, the buffet drawn but not ordered, the art and lamps, the plant; no rug (F-66).
Total $1,505.86: placed $1,444.93 + extras $60.93; prices as of 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-26 (those before today price-stale, F-02).
Flags across the layout: tight:26 (the wall side, F-36).
